verification_method: Official PDFs downloaded from meity.gov.in and static.pib.gov.in on 2026-10-08 and read directly. General web search was used only to locate official URLs; no user document was ever sent to a search service.
important_note: Effective dates for the 'eighteen months' and 'one year' phases are computed from the Gazette notification date (13 November 2025). The e-Gazette upload identifier carries 14 November 2025 and PIB describes the Rules as notified on 14 November 2025, so the exact commencement day should be re-checked by a qualified reviewer. This registry does not make compliance determinations.

sources.title: Notification G.S.R. 843(E) appointing commencement dates for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
sources.summary: On publication: s.1(2), s.2, ss.18-26, s.35, ss.38-43, s.44(1) and (3). One year after publication: s.6(9) and s.27(1)(d). Eighteen months after publication: ss.3-5, s.6(1)-(8) and (10), ss.7-17, s.27 (except (1)(d)), ss.28-34, 36, 37 and s.44(2).
sources.applicability_notes: Controls which DPDP Act duties are in force on a given date.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (No. 22 of 2023), section 4 - Grounds for processing personal data
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; published by the Ministry of Law and Justice (Legislative Department); text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: Personal data may be processed for a lawful purpose either with the Data Principal's consent or for 'certain legitimate uses' (section 7). Consent is therefore not the only ground.
sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). Use to explain that not all processing depends on consent.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 5 - Notice
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: A consent request must be accompanied or preceded by a notice describing the personal data and purpose, how to exercise withdrawal and grievance rights, and how to complain to the Board; option to access the notice in English or an Eighth Schedule language.
sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). Applies to consent requests, not to processing on other grounds.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 6 - Consent
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: Consent must be free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action, limited to data necessary for the specified purpose (6(1)); illustration: contact-list access is not necessary for a telemedicine service. Withdrawal must be comparable in ease to giving consent (6(4)).
sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). Relevant only where consent is the basis of processing.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 6(9) - Registration of Consent Managers
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: Every Consent Manager must be registered with the Data Protection Board.
sources.applicability_notes: Commences one year after G.S.R. 843(E). Rarely relevant to a consumer reading a single app notice.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 7 - Certain legitimate uses
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: Lists uses for which processing may occur without consent, including where a person voluntarily provides data for a specified purpose and has not objected (7(a)), and other listed situations.
sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). ConsentGuard does not decide whether a specific use qualifies.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 8(7) - Erasure
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: Unless retention is necessary to comply with law, personal data must be erased on withdrawal of consent or once it is reasonable to assume the specified purpose is no longer served, whichever is earlier.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 11 - Right to access information
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: A Data Principal who gave consent may request a summary of personal data processed and the identities of other Data Fiduciaries and Data Processors with whom it was shared.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, section 13 - Right of grievance redressal
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India; text hosted by MeitY
sources.summary: A Data Principal has the right to readily available means of grievance redressal provided by the Data Fiduciary.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 (G.S.R. 846(E))
sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
sources.summary: Rules 1, 2 and 17-21 in force on publication; Rule 4 one year after publication; Rules 3, 5-16, 22 and 23 eighteen months after publication.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, rule 3 - Notice given by Data Fiduciary
sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
sources.summary: The notice must be understandable independently of other information; give in clear and plain language an itemised description of personal data and the specified purpose(s); and give a link and other means to withdraw consent with ease comparable to giving it, exercise rights, and complain to the Board.
sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after publication of the Rules.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025, rule 8 - Time period for specified purpose deemed no longer served
sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India
sources.summary: Specified classes of Data Fiduciaries must erase data after periods set in the Third Schedule (with 48-hour prior intimation); all Data Fiduciaries must retain processing logs and associated data for at least one year for purposes in the Seventh Schedule.
sources.applicability_notes: Commences eighteen months after publication of the Rules. Note the one-year minimum log retention: a notice that mentions retaining some records for a year is not necessarily over-retention.

sources.title: DPDP Rules, 2025 Notified - A Citizen-Centric Framework for Privacy Protection and Responsible Data Use
sources.issuing_authority: Press Information Bureau, Government of India
sources.summary: Official plain-language explainer: Rules notified 14 November 2025; eighteen-month phased compliance; rights to access, correct, erase and nominate; 90-day response period for requests.
sources.applicability_notes: Government explainer; useful context but not controlling law.

sources.title: Information Technology Act, 2000, section 43A and the IT (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011
sources.issuing_authority: Parliament of India / Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
sources.summary: Verified only indirectly: DPDP Act s.44(2)(a) omits IT Act s.43A, and s.44(2) commences eighteen months after G.S.R. 843(E). The current text and scope of s.43A and the SPDI Rules were NOT retrieved or verified in this build.
sources.applicability_notes: Do not cite as a verified legal finding. A qualified reviewer should confirm the current interim position.
